heard: Undocking to escape a violent spin made Armstrong's capsule spin faster. Most people assume separating from a target vehicle instantly solves a docking emergency. On March 16, 1966, astronauts Neil Armstrong and David Scott launched on the Gemini 8 mission. After completing the first United States space docking, a thruster short-circuited and stuck open. The combined spacecraft entered an uncontrolled rotation, reaching nearly one revolution per second. Threatened with blacking out, Armstrong shut down the orbital thrusters and fired the reentry control system. That emergency maneuver used 75% of their emergency fuel to stabilize the ship. Undocking to escape a violent spin made Armstrong's capsule spin faster.
